## WhyAIsometimesgetsitwrong—andbigstridestoaddressit
byVanessaHo

To target this phenomenon, known as “hallucinations,” they created a text-retrieval task that would give most humans a headache and then tracked and improved the models’ responses.

Technically, hallucinations are “ungrounded” content, which means a model has changed the data it’s been given or added additional information not contained in it.

That’s why Microsoft has created a comprehensive array of tools to help address ungroundedness based on expertise from developing its own AI products like [Microsoft Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot).

“The model is amazing at reasoning over information, but we don’t think it should be the source of the answer,” says Bird.

Click here to load media

“There is a fundamental question: Why do they hallucinate? she says.

Kamar says LLMs tend to hallucinate more around facts that are less available in internet training data, making the attention study an important step in understanding the mechanisms and impact of ungrounded content.

“As AI systems support people with critical tasks and information-sharing, we have to take every risk that these systems generate very seriously, because we are trying to build future AI systems that will do good things in the world,” she says.

_Learn more about_ [_Microsoft’s Responsible AI work._](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/ai/responsible-ai)

# Solving the Very-Real Problem of AI Hallucination
## Fast Facts on AI Hallucinations
- AI hallucinations are false or misleading outputs generated by models. These responses sound correct but lack factual grounding, posing risks in enterprise environments especially in the legal, pharmaceutical, and financial sectors.
- Copilot tools are especially prone to hallucinations when disconnected from real-time enterprise data or when designed with weak prompts.

## Why Hallucinations Are a Significant Risk in Enterprise AI
In modern enterprises, reasonable-sounding but incorrect AI outputs  are trusted and acted on by employees every day.These can lead to potential compliance violations and miscalculations in business decisions. These hallucinations can also be problematic when embedded in semantic search, RAG tools, and AI copilots.

However, if these systems retrieve irrelevant or low-quality documents, the AI may generate hallucinated outputs based on this faulty context.

## What’s Next?
One of the most serious risks is oversharing, when copilots confidently reveal irrelevant, unauthorized, or even confidential information.

## FAQ
An AI hallucination occurs when a model generates a factually incorrect, fabricated, or misleading response that often sounds  reasonable.

Copilot hallucinations typically come from weak grounding in enterprise data or outdated LLM knowledge. Without clear access to authoritative sources or retrieval constraints, copilots fill in the gaps, often incorrectly.
